> OXBOW is a research prototype that analyzes historical, de-identified data only. It does not process live financial transactions, does not trade or advise on any financial instrument, does not make real financial decisions, and is not financial advice. Monetary figures are model estimates derived from stated assumptions, not measured outcomes. Results are not validated for operational use by any financial institution.

## Headline

- PR-AUC (primary) **0.059115 (source: `out/backtest/model_card.json#headline/pr_auc` · provenance: `measured`)**, bootstrap 95 % CI [0.003833, 0.128822].
- AUROC is reported for comparability only and is deliberately de-emphasised: on a 0.1019 % base rate it is not the number that decides anything.
- Headline corpus `real-corpus`; model version `d1fe7798e6ff`; feature-spec hash `b622c5f6ca1fc41a…`.
- Band note carried with the figure: Recovery-rate band r in 0.35 (sensitivity over r=0.20/0.35/0.50 per config/economics.yaml)
- Net benefit of the headline configuration: 2,586,701.82 UGX (out/backtest/model_card.json#headline/net_benefit_total_minor).
- **Provenance: `real_corpus`.** Figures came from a real per-account corpus run through the P4b scorer, the P5 allocator and the ONE splits module; provenance=real_corpus.

## Walk-forward design

- Scheme `expanding_window_temporal`; shuffling: **no** — temporal, never random, because a random split on transaction data is the classic tell.
- Embargo 30 (source: `out/backtest/model_card.json#embargo_days` · provenance: `measured`) days = longest feature lookback 30 (source: `out/backtest/model_card.json#max_lookback_days` · provenance: `measured`). The embargo exists because a 30-day rolling feature computed just after a boundary would otherwise see training-period data.
- Folds supplied: 5 (source: `out/backtest/model_card.json#walk_forward/corpus_feasibility/folds_supplied` · provenance: `measured`); corpus span offered: 717.6352 (source: `out/backtest/model_card.json#walk_forward/corpus_feasibility/corpus_span_days` · provenance: `measured`); supports a literal walk-forward at that embargo: **yes (source: `out/backtest/model_card.json#walk_forward/corpus_feasibility/supports_literal_walk_forward` · provenance: `measured`)**.
- If supports_literal_walk_forward is False the run is reported as a single-holdout (or on a corpus whose window the embargo fits), never as a 5-fold result invented from an insufficient timeline. The IBM-AML 18-day window against a 30-day embargo is exactly this case (DEV-013).
- All figures are per corpus. PaySim (tabular/volume, Module A) and IBM-AML (network/typology, Module B) are reported separately and never averaged into one headline (DEV-011/DEV-013, plan §6).

Source for every cell: `out/backtest/model_card.json#/ablation_table` (source: `out/backtest/ablation_results.json#provenance_note` · provenance: `measured`). Rows the harness expected: `rules_only`, `scorecard_only`, `gbm_no_graph`, `gbm_with_graph`, `plus_ifusion`, `full_calibrated`, `threshold_vs_ev`, `full_on_ibm`.

**What this table does not measure:** Every honest arm here runs the full fitted stack; the rows differ by policy ladder, not yet by feature subset or model. A scientifically distinct ablation (scorecard-only vs GBM-without-graph vs GBM-with-graph) needs per-row feature subsetting, which is named here rather than faked by reusing one scorer's numbers under eight labels.

## The leakage control is a test, not a boast

- A deliberately lookahead-leaking configuration is included as a control and must win. Detected: **yes (source: `out/backtest/ablation_results.json#leakage_control/detected` · provenance: `measured`)**, control PR-AUC 1 (source: `out/backtest/ablation_results.json#leakage_control/control_pr_auc` · provenance: `measured`) against best honest 0.059115 (source: `out/backtest/ablation_results.json#leakage_control/best_honest_pr_auc` · provenance: `measured`).
- leakage control detected as expected: control PR-AUC 1.0 exceeds the best honest arm 0.05911523052214634, proving the harness can see lookahead.

## Statistical hygiene

- Configurations evaluated: 9 (source: `9`); selection on `validation`; test fold touched exactly once: **True** at `2026-09-27T19:29:18+00:00`.
- 9 configurations were evaluated against this corpus; with N configurations tried the best validation result is optimistically biased, which is exactly why the headline figure is taken from the untouched test fold and not from the validation peak.
- Seed stability is published as mean ± sd across the configured seeds, never as the best of five.
- Monte Carlo: interval=[0.05, 0.95], max_depth=4, runs=10,000, seed=1,337 — the seed and the draw count are stored with the interval so a quoted tail can be reproduced or challenged.
- MLflow logged: **no (source: `False`)** (no tracking URI supplied (degraded, not failed)). Degraded, not failed: `run_id`, the feature-spec hash and the artifact digests still pin what produced each number.

## Fairness and robustness

- Neither corpus carries a protected attribute (payee/payer identifiers are salted hashes and no gender, age-band, ethnicity, nationality or account-holder-type field is present in PaySim or IBM-AML), so a demographic fairness table cannot be computed honestly. The check is run anyway against the realistic over-flagging proxies in this domain: transaction amount, account age, activity volume and community size.
- Proxy axes actually tested: `amount_minor` (4 buckets), `account_age_days` (2 buckets), `activity_volume` (0 buckets, reason: axis 'activity_volume' has fewer than 4 non-null values in this corpus), `community_size` (0 buckets, reason: axis 'community_size' has fewer than 4 non-null values in this corpus).
- Perturbations: amount_shift_minus10={'reordered_at_cutoff': False, 'shift_ratio': -0.1, 'spearman': 0.99998418}, amount_shift_plus10={'reordered_at_cutoff': False, 'shift_ratio': 0.1, 'spearman': 0.99998629}, edge_drop_typology_recall={'caveat': "recall recomputed on a seeded 90 % subsample of the fold's labelled test rows; the full drop-10%-of-EDGES-and-recompute-graph-features variant needs the P3 graph layer and is a named dependency, not this proxy", 'drop_ratio': 0.1, 'max_abs_shift': 0.0, 'per_typology': [], 'seed': 1337}
- Risk-adjusted benefit ratio is **not a Sharpe ratio**: no risk-free rate is subtracted and there is no annualisation; it is a mean-over-std ratio of per-fold net benefit, shown with its formula Formula: `mean(per-period net benefit) / std(per-period net benefit)`, value 0.4472136.

## Drift

**Not published.** This section needs `out/warehouse/drift_period`, produced by `oxbow.scoring.drift via the warehouse handoff` (stage P4b). It will carry:
  - PSI and per-bin CSI per feature per period (oxbow.scoring.drift)
  - score PSI by period, and the worst value that triggers the action
  - the degrade threshold from config/model.yaml :: drift.psi_action (0.25)
  - the named reason the run degraded to rules-plus-scorecard

No PSI value is printed until the artifact exists: a drift table generated from intent would report stability that was never measured, and the action at drift.psi_action is the reason the number matters.
